correctness.rationale: The homogeneous degree-n Bargmann–Fock compression has eigenvalue Beta(k+1,n-k+1) mass on [a,b], with total beta shape n+2 and binomial tail parameter m=n+1. Under common-uniform monotone coupling B_a≤B_b, the random index interval I=[B_a,B_b) has P(k∈I)=λ_k, proving exactly V=1/2 E|I_1△I_2| for independent copies. For sqrt(m)(b-a)→c finite at interior t, the rescaled two interval starts converge to independent σ-normal locations while their lengths converge to c in L². The symmetric-difference length is continuous and endpoint differences have uniform L² bounds, giving E[min(c,σ|Z_1-Z_2|)] and its erfc integral H_t(c). For c→∞, overlap probability tends to one as lengths grow faster than fluctuations; the endpoint difference CLT yields H_t(∞)=2σ/√π. H prime erfc and H double-prime negative follow directly. Independent finite exact binomial trace calculations at m=7,20,100,250 verified normalization and defects; no finite check substitutes for CLT or uniform integrability.

value.rationale: A projective latitude band has two quantum interfaces whose fluctuations become coupled precisely at width O(n^-1/2). The explicit strictly concave H_t(c) quantifies their nonadditivity and connects vanished width to the twice-single-boundary constant. The finite exact coupled-binomial symmetric-difference identity is useful beyond the limiting regime; this is an analytically motivated spectral concentration problem, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
